title: The Water in This Cloud Weighs 500 Tonnes #science #nature
description:
The water in a puffy cumulus cloud about a kilometre across weighs about 500 tonnes. The cloud holds about half a gram of liquid water in each cubic metre; over a billion cubic metres that adds up to 500,000 kg. It floats because the droplets are tiny (about a hundredth of a millimetre), so they fall very slowly, and rising air holds them up. (The air inside the cloud weighs far more; it is not counted here.)

More sky physics: Why is the sky blue but sunsets red? https://youtu.be/H_61WImrwoQ

Sources
- USGS Water Science School, How much does a cloud weigh? (usgs.gov)
- Wallace, J. M. & Hobbs, P. V. (2006), Atmospheric Science: An Introductory Survey, 2nd ed., chapter 6 (cloud droplets and fall speeds)
